evidence: PILOT-001-R3-001 reproduces false hash mismatches for legitimate RED blobs between the 10 KB generic Git cap and the 1 MB file limit.
Canonical containment, link rejection, clean committed metadata, ancestry, and redacted diagnostics were inspected without a separate candidate-scope security finding.
PILOT-001-R3-001 and PILOT-001-R3-002 violate the exact evidence and mandatory acceptance contracts.
Bounded subprocess consumption exists, but its generic 10 KB cap is incompatible with the permitted 1 MB RED blob contract.
The shared lifecycle policy materially reduces duplication and no separate actionable maintainability issue was found.
PILOT-001-R3-002 leaves frozen-test retention unenforced, and the source-shape output-bound test misses the large-blob interaction.

findings.expectedBehavior: Every declared RED blob up to the accepted one-megabyte file limit is hashed completely, or a limited read produces an accurate output-limit diagnostic.
findings.observedBehavior: The generic ten-kilobyte Git output cap truncates larger permitted blobs; the validator ignores the limited result and hashes only the prefix as a false content mismatch.
findings.reproduction: Run deno task ticket:validate docs/planning/tickets/PILOT-001; legitimate 23-89 KB RED blobs report content_hash_mismatch.
findings.impact: The validator cannot validate its own canonical packet and categorically rejects correct evidence between 10,001 bytes and one megabyte.
findings.requiredRemediation: Read declared blobs with a limit derived from the already-checked blob size, check success and limit state before hashing, and preserve accurate diagnostics.
findings.verification: Add valid and wrong-hash fixtures above ten kilobytes plus near-limit and truly oversized cases; the canonical ticket command must pass when review state is otherwise valid.

findings.expectedBehavior: Every exact frozen RED test or deterministic check remains unchanged in the reviewed descendant candidate.
findings.observedBehavior: The validator hashes tests only at redRevision and permits an in-scope candidate to delete or replace those blobs.
findings.reproduction: Create a valid RED commit, delete or modify its declared test in the candidate, keep the correct RED digest, and validate with that path inside allowedWrites.
findings.impact: A candidate can remove the regression that established RED and still manufacture compliant TDD evidence.
findings.requiredRemediation: Require every frozen RED test/check blob to exist unchanged at candidateRevision or add an explicit separately content-addressed later-test protocol.
findings.verification: Add candidate deletion, modification, skip/exclusion, and unchanged-test Git fixtures.

notes: Protected configuration authority and baseline-versus-candidate task definitions remain dependent bootstrap gaps for a separate ticket; they are not additional candidate-scope findings in this review.
